title: Derived sum evaluation at the coefficient unit
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $e:U\to X$ a separated etale finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $T=e^*$ for exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $L=e_{\Sigma!}$ for sheafified lift-indexed sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], and $S=D(L)\dashv T$ for its termwise derived adjunction with sum/evaluation counit $\operatorname{ev}$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Put $\mathbf1_X=A_X$ and $\mathbf1_U=A_U$, constant sheaves placed in degree zero [def-kun-constant-sheaf], and let $u:T\mathbf1_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_U$ be the canonical coefficient-unit comparison [def-pur-etale-exact-pullback-unit-composition-comparisons]. Use derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], its left unitor $\lambda$, and the natural derived sum projection
$$p^\Sigma_{M,K}:SM\otimes_A^LK\xrightarrow{\sim}S(M\otimes_A^LTK),$$
specified on total tensor representatives by $(s,m)\otimes k\mapsto(s,m\otimes s^*k)$ [lem-pur-etale-sum-tensor-totalization, lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat]. Define $a_K=\lambda_{TK}\circ(u\otimes1_{TK})$. Then, for every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\operatorname{ev}_K\circ S(a_K)\circ p^\Sigma_{T\mathbf1_X,K}=\lambda_K\circ(\operatorname{ev}_{\mathbf1_X}\otimes1_K).$$
This is an equality of derived natural transformations from $S(T\mathbf1_X)\otimes_A^L(-)$ to the identity functor. On sheaves the same equality holds with ordinary tensor, the sheaf projection $p^0$ of [lem-pur-etale-sheaf-projection-map], and the sheaf sum/restriction counit: for every module sheaf $H$,
$$\operatorname{ev}^0_H\circ L(a_H)\circ p^0_{T\mathbf1_X,H}=\lambda_H\circ(\operatorname{ev}^0_{\mathbf1_X}\otimes1_H).$$
The derived counit is the image of termwise sheaf evaluation under localization, and the displayed derived equality agrees with this sheaf equality on complexes of flat terms that are K-flat. No boundedness, constructibility, coefficient finiteness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First fix the coefficient and restriction identifications. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], on an etale test object $(W,s)$ over $U$ the underlying abelian sheaf $TH$ is $H(W)$, and the inverse-image unit is restriction. Its $A$-action is the inverse image of the action by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so this is also the module restriction identification. The section denoted $s^*h$ in the projection formula becomes $h$: the projection $W\times_XU\to W$ followed by its graph section is the identity. The constant-ring comparison sends a constant section $a$ to the same $a$ by that proposition, hence does so for all sections locally. Its degree-zero localization is precisely the specified $u$: [def-pur-etale-exact-pullback-unit-composition-comparisons] defines $u$ using the exact/left-derived comparison, while [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] identifies the canonical left-derived unit comparison with pullback of the degree-zero ring complex. Composing with the inverse exact/left-derived comparison cancels that comparison. Thus the sheaf coefficient map $u^0:T A_X\to A_U$ and its localization are the coefficient maps used in the two assertions.

source.place: Step 1, canonical coefficient-unit identification for etale normalization; agent expansion using the cited normalized comparisons

proof.text: Prove the sheaf equality before deriving. The stipulated sum/evaluation counit is induced on the presenting sum of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] by $i_s(x)\mapsto x$ under Step 1. Indeed a map out of that sum is specified by its summand maps; the identity on the restricted sheaf has these very summand maps, so its adjoint is evaluation. Unique factorization through module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives the stated counit. For a local generator $(s,a)\otimes h$ of $L(TA_X)\otimes_A H$, [lem-pur-etale-sheaf-projection-map] gives $(s,a\otimes s^*h)$. Applying $L(a_H)$ and then evaluation gives $ah$ under Step 1. The other composite first evaluates $(s,a)$ to $a$, and the left unitor then gives $ah$ as well. The unitors are the action maps by [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints]. Linearity proves equality on the presenting direct sums and pure tensors. The tensor is sheafification of the presheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; sections of either sheafification are locally represented by presenting sections. Hence the two sheaf maps agree, including on locally glued sections, by the uniqueness clause of module sheafification. The formulas commute with restriction and every module map $H\to H'$, so this is an equality of natural transformations.

proof.text: The coefficient sheaf $A_X$ is flat because its tensor action unitor identifies $A_X\otimes_A-$ with the identity exact functor. Also $A_X[0]$ is K-flat: its total tensor with an acyclic complex is that same complex via the action unitor, hence acyclic, exactly the definition [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The same reasoning applies on $U$ and to the isomorphic degree-zero complex $T A_X[0]$. The action unitors on complexes and their localizations are supplied by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. By [lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat], $L(T A_X)[0]$ is flat termwise and K-flat. Now take an arbitrary complex $C$ representing $K$. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ with $P$ K-flat and flat termwise. This is valid on the small etale site with its constant commutative-ring sheaf and imposes no boundedness. Derived tensors with these coefficient complexes and $K$ are therefore computed by their ordinary total tensors with $P$, as in [def-kun-derived-tensor].

source.place: Tag 0GKF, lemma-f-shriek-projection, followed by agent K-flat representative reduction using the cited unbounded resolution theorem

proof.text: Apply Step 2 in every degree to $H=P^n$. The source total tensor has only the coefficient degree $0$ in its first factor; its degree $n$ is $L(T A_X)\otimes_A P^n$. By [lem-pur-etale-sum-tensor-totalization], the chain projection has exactly the sheaf generator formula used in Step 2 on each such summand. The coefficient comparison is Step 1, and the chain unitors are the action maps, whose localizations are the derived unitors by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Thus the two chain maps from this total tensor to $P$ coincide in every degree by Step 2. The differential is respected since all maps are natural in the sheaf argument; there is no extra sign because the coefficient degree is $0$. For the counit, use the specified termwise adjunction $S\dashv T$ of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. The exact-derived-adjunction construction [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] localizes the degreewise original counit. Exactness of $L$ and $T$ therefore makes the localized chain map precisely $\operatorname{ev}$, rather than a new choice of adjunction counit. On the models of Step 3 the specified $p^\Sigma$, $S(a_K)$ and the right-hand tensor of evaluation are consequently represented by the very chain maps just compared. Localizing their equality proves the displayed derived identity at $QP$.

source.place: Step 1, etale sum/restriction counit normalization; agent termwise passage of the Tag 0GKF calculation to unbounded total tensors

proof.text: Finally $QP\to K$ is an isomorphism. Naturality of the specified projection, counit, coefficient map, tensor and unitors transports the equality at $QP$ to $K$: postcompose the two sides with $QP\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ and use their naturality squares, then cancel the induced source isomorphism. This proves every component, hence the equality of derived natural transformations. For maps between flat-term K-flat models the equality is already the chain equality of Step 4, and it remains so upon inversion of quasi-isomorphisms. The equivalence from the localization of flat-term K-flat models to the derived category in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] ensures these compute the same derived tensor and are independent of the models. This also proves the stipulated agreement with sheaf evaluation on such complexes. All resolutions and sum/tensor comparisons used above are unbounded ones. No finite coefficient, constructibility, Noetherian, or boundedness assumption has entered.

I checked the identity on generators: both sides send (s,a)⊗h to a·h, since s*h=h (restriction along the graph composed with the projection is the identity, lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction (2)). It also holds for e=id, U empty, U=X⊔X, A=0 and A=Z/4. Step 1: u=Q(c), because the definition's exact/left-derived comparison cancels against the R[0]-pullback unit of lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit; prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (1),(2) gives c and the module action. Step 2: the presenting-sum counit, the projection formula quoted exactly from lem-pur-etale-sheaf-projection-map, unitor a⊗x↦ax (lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints), and equality checked locally then extended by uniqueness of sheafification.
